\label{lemma-base-change-shriek-flat}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^g & Y
}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of $\textit{FTS}_S$ with $g$ flat.
Then there is an isomorphism
$L(g')^* \circ f^! \to (f')^! \circ Lg^*$ on
$D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.

Fix a Noetherian base $S$. Write $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ for separated schemes of finite type over $S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, choose a factorization $f=\bar f\circ j$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ an open immersion and $\bar f:\bar X\to Y$ proper. If $a_{\bar f}$ is the right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$ on unbounded quasi-coherent derived categories, define $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ as $j^*a_{\bar f}$, independently (up to canonical identifications) of the chosen compactification. Suppose
\[
\begin{matrix}X'=X\times_YY'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{matrix}
\]
is a cartesian diagram in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, where $g$ is flat. Then there exists a canonical natural isomorphism of functors $L(g')^*\circ f^!\xrightarrow{\sim}(f')^!\circ Lg^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$. It is obtained by applying derived right-adjoint base change to a proper compactification of $f$ and restricting to $X'$. Flatness of $g$ makes the compactification square Tor-independent.

\label{lemma-good-dualizing-unique}
In Situation \ref{situation-dualizing} let $X$ be a scheme of finite type
over $S$ and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a finite open covering of $X$
by schemes separated over $S$. If there exists a dualizing complex
normalized relative to $\omega_S^\bullet$ and $\mathcal{U}$, then it is unique
up to unique isomorphism.
statement: Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and a dualizing complex $D_S\in D(\mathcal O_S)$. For a finite-type $S$-scheme $T$, choose a finite open covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}$ by $S$-separated schemes, and let $p_i:U_i\to S$. Define $D_i=p_i^!D_S$, using the upper-shriek functors of separated finite-type schemes over $S$. On overlaps $U_{ij}$ their restrictions have canonical comparison isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:D_i|_{U_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_j|_{U_{ij}}$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A *dualizing complex normalized relative to $D_S$ and $\mathcal U$* is a pair $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ with $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ and compatible isomorphisms $\alpha_i:D_T|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_i$, such that $\alpha_j\alpha_i^{-1}=\varphi_{ij}$ on each overlap. The normalized object includes the local identifications, not merely the derived isomorphism class of $D_T$. If two normalized pairs $(D_T,\{\alpha_i\})$ and $(D'_T,\{\alpha'_i\})$ exist for the *same* base complex $D_S$ and covering $\mathcal U$, then there exists a **unique** isomorphism $u:D_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D'_T$ in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ such that $\alpha'_i\circ u|_{U_i}=\alpha_i$ for every $i$. The uniqueness is relative to the specified normalizing isomorphisms, not a claim that the underlying dualizing complex has no automorphisms.

and a coherent Cohen-Macaulay $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\omega_X$
such that $\omega_X^\bullet = \omega_X[-n]$.

\label{lemma-duality-proper-over-field}
Let $X$ be a proper scheme over a field $k$. There exists a dualizing complex
$\omega_X^\bullet$ with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^i(\omega_X^\bullet)$ is nonzero only for $i \in [-\dim(X), 0]$,
\item $\omega_X = H^{-\dim(X)}(\omega_X^\bullet)$ is a coherent
$(S_2)$-module whose support is the irreducible components
of dimension $\dim(X)$,
\item the dimension of the support of $H^i(\omega_X^\bullet)$ is at most $-i$,
\item for $x \in X$ closed the module
$H^i(\omega_{X, x}^\bullet) \oplus \ldots \oplus H^0(\omega_{X, x}^\bullet)$
is nonzero if and only if $\text{depth}(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) \leq -i$,
\item for $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ there are functorial
isomorphisms\footnote{This property
characterizes $\omega_X^\bullet$ in $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$
up to unique isomorphism by the Yoneda lemma. Since $\omega_X^\bullet$
is in $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ in fact it suffices to consider
$K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.}
$$
\Ext^i_X(K, \omega_X^\bullet) = \Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k)
$$
compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles,
\item there are functorial isomorphisms
$\Hom(\mathcal{F}, \omega_X) = \Hom_k(H^{\dim(X)}(X, \mathcal{F}), k)$
for $\mathcal{F}$ quasi-coherent on $X$, and
\item if $X \to \Spec(k)$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$,
then $\omega_X^\bullet \cong \wedge^d\Omega_{X/k}[d]$ and
$\omega_X \cong \wedge^d\Omega_{X/k}$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-determinant}
Let $X$ be a locally ringed space. Let
$$
\mathcal{E}_1 \xrightarrow{\alpha} \mathcal{E}_0 \to \mathcal{F} \to 0
$$
be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.

free of ranks $r_1, r_0$. Then there is a canonical map
$$
\wedge^{r_0 - r_1}\mathcal{F}
\longrightarrow
\wedge^{r_1}(\mathcal{E}_1^\vee) \otimes \wedge^{r_0}\mathcal{E}_0
$$
which is an isomorphism on the stalk at $x \in X$
if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ is locally free of rank $r_0 - r_1$
in an open neighbourhood of $x$.

\label{lemma-lift-map}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
Let $(K_n)$ be a Deligne system and denote
$K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$ the value
of the constant system $(K_n|_U)$. Let $L$ be an object of
$D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Then $\colim \Hom_X(K_n, L) = \Hom_U(K, L|_U)$.
statement:
For a Noetherian scheme $X$, open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and coherent bounded complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$, choose a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ whose vanishing set is $X\setminus U$. Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. Let $(K_n)$ be a Deligne system for $U\subset X$ with common restriction $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$, and let $L\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X)$. Then restriction induces an isomorphism
\[
\operatorname*{colim}_{n}\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(U)}(K,L|_U).
\]
The colimit maps are defined by precomposition with transitions $K_{n+1}\to K_n$, not by passing to an inverse limit.

\label{lemma-extension-by-zero}
Let $j : U \to X$ be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ be Deligne systems.
Let $K$ and $L$ be the values of the constant systems
$(K_n|_U)$ and $(L_n|_U)$. Given a morphism $\alpha : K \to L$
of $D(\mathcal{O}_U)$
there is a unique morphism of pro-systems $(K_n) \to (L_n)$
of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\alpha$.
\item Given $K \in D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U)$ there exists a
Deligne system $(K_n)$ such that $(K_n|_U)$ is constant
with value $K$.
\item The pro-object $(K_n)$ of $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_X)$
of (2) is unique up to unique isomorphism (as a pro-object).
\end{enumerate}

Define $K_n$ as the bounded coherent *subcomplex* with terms $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^q$ and differentials induced by those of $\mathcal F^\bullet$. The inverse system $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$, with maps induced by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F^\bullet\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F^\bullet$, is a *Deligne system* for $j$. Its restriction to $U$ is a constant system in $D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ with value $K=\mathcal F^\bullet|_U$. A *pro-isomorphism* refers to isomorphism in $\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_X))$, whose Hom sets into a constant object $L$ are $\operatorname*{colim}_n\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(X)}(K_n,L)$. For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of Noetherian schemes: (1) if $(K_n)$ and $(L_n)$ are Deligne systems with constant restriction values $K,L$ on $U$, any morphism $\alpha:K\to L$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ extends to a **unique morphism of pro-objects** $(K_n)\to(L_n)$ that restricts to $\alpha$ (not necessarily a levelwise map with matching indices); (2) every $K\in D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^b(\mathcal O_U)$ occurs as the common restriction value of some Deligne system on $X$; and (3) such a pro-object is unique up to the unique pro-isomorphism inducing the identity on $K$. \label{lemma-extension-by-zero-triangle}

$$

are Deligne systems and such that the restriction of these
distinguished triangles to $U$ is isomorphic to the distinguished triangle
we started out with.

\label{lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees-bis}
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a
complex of coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $p \in \mathbf{Z}$.
Set $\mathcal{H} = H^p(\mathcal{F}^\bullet)$ and
$\mathcal{H}_n = H^p(\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{F}^\bullet)$.
Then there are canonical $\mathcal{O}_X$-module maps
$$
\ldots \to \mathcal{H}_3 \to \mathcal{H}_2 \to \mathcal{H}_1 \to \mathcal{H}
$$
There exists a $c > 0$ such that for $n \geq c$ the image of
$\mathcal{H}_n \to \mathcal{H}$ is contained in
$\mathcal{I}^{n - c}\mathcal{H}$ and there is a canonical
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module map
$\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{H} \to \mathcal{H}_{n - c}$ such that the compositions
$$
\mathcal{I}^n \mathcal{H} \to \mathcal{H}_{n - c} \to
\mathcal{I}^{n - 2c}\mathcal{H}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal{H}_n \to \mathcal{I}^{n - c}\mathcal{H} \to \mathcal{H}_{n - 2c}
$$
are the canonical ones. In particular, the inverse systems
$(\mathcal{H}_n)$ and $(\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{H})$
are isomorphic as pro-objects of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

\label{lemma-well-defined-pre}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes.
Let $V \subset Y$ be an open subscheme and set $U = f^{-1}(V)$.

U \ar[r]_j \ar[d]_g & X \ar[d]^f \\
V \ar[r]^{j'} & Y
}
$$
Then we have a canonical isomorphism $Rj'_! \circ Rg_* \to Rf_* \circ Rj_!$
of functors $D^b_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_U) \to

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a *proper* map of Noetherian schemes, let $V\subset Y$ be open, and let $U=f^{-1}(V)$. Write $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $j':V\hookrightarrow Y$, and $g=f|_U:U\to V$ (proper). where $Rf_*$ is applied termwise to coherent pro-objects. Thus coherent pro-extension by zero commutes with proper pushforward in the cartesian open square.

and $L \in D^+_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ we have
$$
\Hom_X(K, f^!L) =
\Hom_{\text{Pro-}D^+_{\textit{Coh}}(\mathcal{O}_Y)}(Rf_!K, L)
$$

Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$; let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of separated schemes of finite type over $S$. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, the *upper shriek* $f^!$ sends $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ and is built from proper compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$ by $j^*a_{\bar f}$, where $a_{\bar f}$ is right adjoint to $R\bar f_*$. \xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Pro}(D_{\mathrm{Coh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y))}(Rf_!K,L).
